purpose: UI state, ownership, persistence and service relationships for future frontend rewrites. This is an engineering design map, not an execution log or a completion claim.

domainRelations.semantics: Rectangular selection, strict quoted TSV and topology context commands share the registered parent draft. Paste respects readonly cells and source validation.
Source feature intersections update the same selected set used by tables. Measurements use world coordinates; final length segments sample real terrain slope with stale-owner rejection.
Saved diagnostics read retained HDF nodes. Unsaved mesh diagnostics use the current child draft; unavailable drafts never fall back to saved cells. Compute writers suspend source reads.
Attribute comparison consumes actual Plan drafts. Matrix generation preserves source option order and holds its mutation lease until actual duplex terminal acknowledgement.
Authentication, clear and URL settings update the shared provider. First-launch secrets stay in memory. Token storage does not invent a missing GPU Hub compute registration.
Actual source providers stage and validate imported projects. Source imports that cannot cancel keep their mutation lease when presentation closes.

Command or Control toggles a true feature set; native list Shift selects a source-ordered range. Replacing or hiding a render owner retires the set. Duplicate source IDs cannot receive edits. Geoprocessing consumes the same captured set.

Result metadata and appended images live in a persistent parent child draft. Save validates the owner, changes a same-directory Result copy using source Plan.Save, preserves unrelated datasets, atomically publishes, and rebases late edits from the receipt. Discard never writes source HDF.

Checkboxes are transient per-map state and resolve the exact input through the source tree before rendering actual projected coordinates. Source geometry joins the common camera bounds. Uncheck and compute start retire pending reads; this state never writes visualization XML.

A writer callback grants a scoped historical reader lease. Project loaders filter every protected HDF before constructing source models, and revision capture filters before hashing. Normal source reconfiguration remains blocked. Only disjoint historical Result runtimes may refresh; the compute process owns live writer frames.

Actual GDAL metadata validates a real TIFF before a checked source map node is published. The first map and layer are one visualization transaction. File connections stay in the normal project draft. Duplicate, stale and foreign-owner requests cannot mutate the map.

Follow mode propagates exact current feature context; pin freezes that reference but never bypasses source invalidation. A Boundary receiver requires the same canonical file, SHA and line identity. Quick Edit closes before validated Add or View callbacks. Feature selection does not invent a profile-index relationship.

Native overlays restore independent keyed placements, preserve unrelated entries, arrange same-corner peers and retain runtime z order. First-launch application-data suppression passes no serialization key and performs no placement reads or writes.

First-launch uses transient defaults and UID without clearing persisted application data. Ordinary launches reuse the retained UID key. Initial project and crash origin remain explicit launch inputs. Binary stream mode must consume the actual source protocol rather than interpret arbitrary JSON as a map.

Force-set and clear use actual selected source property objects or the topology undo ledger. Live validation replays the captured read-only source state and accepts messages only while text, selection and all owner tokens still match. Geometry output is committed only by parent Save.

The runtime factor scales pen and marker dimensions across map, minimap, boundary and geometry views. It never changes world coordinates, camera scale, persisted source symbology or source unit values. Pure style helpers receive an explicit factor.

Categories and service version come from the retained report endpoint. Previewed report fields and attachments retain exact source ownership. The bounded Modules inventory is collected by the .NET backend process from loaded managed assemblies and enumerated native modules; file-backed modules carry SHA-256 when readable, and the Swift frontend process image is excluded. Local geometry capture verifies canonical asset membership and revisions; submission happens only through the explicit native report action.

Actual query product boundaries share the map transform. The smallest boundary supplies hit metadata and overlap identities. Terrain annotations require an idle primary tool and no Shift modifier, and stale sheets cannot clear a newer owner overlay.

Typed split/node/vertex/mask/metadata operations replay retained source commands. Original outer/hole rings feed even-odd drawing and hit testing. Parent Save owns persistence; stale responses cannot install a different draft.

Readiness uses Plan and exact dirty Geometry/Boundary drafts in the same source Project graph. Ambiguous owners, pending edits, changed revisions and stale replies fail. Inspection never saves or executes queued Prepare.

Wheel zoom preserves the pointer world coordinate using retained factors. Transient editing gates wheel input. Real projection units and ellipsoid metadata drive coordinates and scale. Descriptor help is separate from USGS feature-hit tooltips.

Actual selected import files populate multi-context metadata. Mixed-value ForceSet edits temporary source-equivalent DTOs and never pretends to mutate files or import parameters not consumed by the retained source.

Transient options pass through the actual map.associations.load rendering route. Toggle cancels old frames and invalidates its context token. Original valid/tiled-raster boundaries are painted by the retained renderer; no visualization XML write.

Actual .NET culture-sensitive parsing returns canonical date or TimeSpan components. Async replies revalidate draft ownership; invalid text stays a presentation draft. Existing setters retain original storage/offset/fraction semantics.

Inspector resolves exact visible source rows and typed payloads, with no same-name joins or active-map fallback. Actual selected raster options and supported component actions retain their source owner.
Source menu opens a virtualized editable 1000-by-1000 zero-valued grid and Add Row/Column actions. It is independent of project/solver data.

Query and download use retained source services; selected opaque IDs are re-queried before downloading. The parent receives raw TIFFs with the exact helper Float scale, uses Custom scale with source ThirtySeconds/stitch defaults, and stages through the existing importer. Seventeen-digit locale text preserves scale bits. Cleanup waits until conversion is idle and validates the captured owner; failures retain a retry token in the editor. Original geographic hit-testing/preview and cancellable query remain unported.

domainRelations.source: Terrain channel/levee source rows and selected detail properties
domainRelations.semantics: A table snapshot is not an edit log. Requests carry only explicitly edited row/column IDs; source validation reads their values from the exact submitted rows and leaves other stale row values untouched. Selection is navigation state, scoped to the current input and actual selected feature/property identities. Changing input first stages the previous input draft, then clears its ephemeral selection. Canonical source replies acknowledge applied row cells and selection-scoped fields so old content-derived IDs are not resent; rebased selection acknowledgements refer only to captured source objects. The original discard baseline remains distinct. Detail fields and table cells share the staged parent save without implicit HDF writes.

Selection invalidates the request even when it is navigation only. Actual full-layer samples are dimmed with retained CloneRatioSaturation(.5,.5), with the selected resampler above them in the same world frame. Clearing selection restores full saturation. Original direct ColorMaps.NLCD2011 behavior and its compact-ID color-domain boundary are preserved.

Copied classifications and XY/XYZ/XYM/XYZM ordinate strings enter an exact polygon input after preview. A validated batch is one undo operation; redo retains feature IDs and later class edits. Stale input or malformed batch cannot mutate source files; explicit parent save publishes it. The typed feature clipboard is separate from whole-layer copying and does not claim external generic polygon clipboard compatibility.

Typed source messages retain duplicate entries and ordered log data, separately from progress text and terminal OperationResult summaries. Headless source collection updates use one serialized synchronization context in place of the Windows UI dispatcher, so concurrent reporter callbacks cannot corrupt collection order. Context switches retire the old list; wrong-owner or noncontiguous updates are rejected.

Only uniquely resolved source associations produce targets. File hashes run in cancellable background chunks before opening and selecting. Model-change Save/Discard/Cancel remains authoritative. Flow-area and boundary-line source indices plus names and revisions resolve current runtime row IDs; late responses never select a fallback. Rendered navigation needs separate native acceptance.

Particles consume actual source vx/vy/magnitude and the Result map transform. Source/profile/viewport/reader-lease changes cancel stale fields and restart motion, respecting reduced motion. adds actual Wind-child field sampling and writer-owned live velocity callbacks with exact map/run/profile/time/viewport guards. Retained Point resampling remains unavailable; live sampling supports one FlowAreaLayer. Native workflow acceptance is separate.

Export captures the unique current Terrain draft with supported rows and selected property context; independent unsaved drafts are rejected. Actual source extent, projection, cell size and overview writer produce the TIFF. Source cancellation may retain an explicitly reported partial output. Export never implicitly saves parent HDF or project XML.

A physical source is read once only when all map nodes agree on its revision. The mixed reader handles GeoJSON and actual retained Shapefile records; Shapefile sidecar families and accepted layers publish atomically, preserving source XY/Z/M and typed attributes. Projected files require actual source/target CRS; valid Local sources retain source coordinates explicitly. Progress counts actual completed files; canceled or superseded batches cannot install. Draft ledgers remain independent.

The actual local raster import sheet exposes each timestamp and component with its overlapping source candidates. Explicit source choices preserve source revision identity, preview actual selected pixels and enter the existing grid import/parent save pipeline. Source issue times determine latest/earliest choices when available; input/display names do not establish identity. Cumulus has its own source-backed per-valid-time issue selection and exact spatial-editor draft save contract. Live authentication/COG acceptance and product footprint rendering remain separate unfinished work.

The source OSM style service and gzip TMS tiles are decoded into project-world paths and labels; retained satellite and USGS network pyramid renderers supply real raster pixels. Native Canvas draws those payloads beneath project content. Invalid local CRS and unavailable services produce explicit diagnostics. Reopening a canceled viewport retries its render; obsolete responses cannot replace the current map. Exact font pixels and original Windows renderer composition are not claimed.

Background settings publish to the exact source map only after an external-change check. Unknown XML survives. Pending Views remain local drafts instead of being incidentally published by an immediate map preference update. Independent source toggles survive the master switch. Additional OSM style/density/label and byte opacity settings use presentation-independent XML keys.

A duplex compute process renders its own retained Result object after actual profiles are written and sends real RGBA frames. Viewport/slot/profile changes replace subscriptions; current run and exact target identity gate every frame. The application does not open another reader on the active HDF writer and never fabricates a file SHA for transient output. Terminal state retires live requests before stable HDF rendering resumes.

Information, Trace, Debug, Warning and Error are represented explicitly. Each retained message action is data bound to a current project and exact editor asset or map UUID; stale history and re-opened project sessions cannot navigate to a new owner accidentally. Hover-paused expiry, explicit dismissal and copy remain native UI behavior.

The native prompt invokes the retained source backup operation, preserves source Geometry and project bytes, adopts source unique-filename behavior for duplicate names and refreshes the catalog to discover the actual created backup. Cancel does not invoke a write. Source changes reject stale requests.

Solver descriptions are supplied from the retained CPU/GPU source helper and native choice metadata. Seven tolerance titles carry their own project units. Presentation localization does not translate field routes, raw enum IDs, file schema or unit symbols. Hardware discovery alone does not imply that a Windows GPU solver executes on macOS.

Split, Merge and Offset previews use retained source geometry algorithms; apply recomputes and checks the same captured inputs and output identities in the existing child ledger. Generated barrel rows retain source default hydraulic attributes, while unmerged original rows preserve identity. SmartAdd samples the actual associated terrain and runs retained ridge pathfinding; endpoint, viewport, options and draft changes invalidate late previews. Accepted segments finish through the same child mutation and parent HDF save. Committing a child draft clears positional selections before reloading the new revision so a reassigned FID cannot select another object. Source-disabled Snap and DeepConnect are not replaced with fake commands.

A true computeStarted Result may be selected before a stable HDF exists. Live logical choices have no invented source SHA and never enter the file-backed source protocol. Slot zero identifies its actual run keyframe; unreadable values do not fall back to an older Result. Raster layer membership comes from exact Result path and revision joins to source selectionIndices. Any unresolved live slot withholds only its own cached presentation, conservatively hiding unassigned layers while preserving unrelated slots and the slot-zero timeline. The raw cache is never presented as new live output. Terminal reconciliation requires the same actual path and source revision, including readable partial output after failure or cancellation. Exact source confirmation also retires the same global terminal run so persisted status becomes authoritative. Only slot zero can replace the keyframe; other live slots retain their own status without replacing it. Profile metadata and raster payload readiness are separate states.

The writer emits bounded incremental metadata directly from its in-memory source event after storing each profile, without opening its writing HDF or guessing from solver progress. Indexed packets can fill out-of-order holes and repeat identical values; conflicting entries are rejected. These real names and times do not claim raster sample availability. Streaming render values and complete native interaction remain separate acceptance requirements.

The detail panels operate on the same MapState and real map selection routes as the canvas. Add prefers the first unselected ordered source Result; Remove retains at least one slot. Source choices carry stable persisted summaries and evaluated diagnostics. A real compute callback can supply a run-bound logical selection before its Result HDF is readable, only for its exact owner Plan and project. It stays separate from stable stored choices; no source SHA is invented. Writer leases suspend source requests but retain accepted choices; per-row status never comes from a group-level aggregate.

The selected saved map supplies its checked terrain and Result contexts. Exact selected arc/barrel polylines and single generic map-vector components are densified and sampled by retained source resamplers. Linked mode replaces base Result sources with whole-group keyed frames, retaining checked base terrain. Missing samples remain gaps; summary sentinels never become ordinary frames. Terrain always uses an elevation axis; Result quantities and distinct unit labels use separate native chart facets with a common station range and synchronized hover, without converting source values. Hover uses returned cumulative distances and densified points; only the owning plot may move or clear its map markers.

The real computeStarted callback supplies the Result path and name before its HDF is readable. A transient catalog row projects that exact run without opening the solver-writing HDF and merges by canonical path when the saved catalog contains it. Terminal state requires matching source identity and revision. Project changes retire rows; actual compute leases block conflicting source reads and writes. Persisted unknown, success and failure remain distinct.

The map Result slot opens actual whole-Plan candidates and activates an accepted composite on that same MapState and canvas. Profiles share the retained keyed timeline. Returning restores the original source selections without serializing the transient composite into .vis. Project, map or source-context replacement cancels pending work and retires the linked context.

The topology Quad entry opens the existing mesh child draft in a native sheet. Its exact side-arc hover preview, dimension edits and resize operations share the normal parent Geometry save. Per-region resolution failures withhold incomplete geometry, disable mutations and expose diagnostics plus retry in that same draft.

Capture source revisions before Project loads its HDFs, then bind actual loaded objects and materialize source code, severity, evaluated message and log data. Revalidate only attached sources. Missing diagnostics, read failure, changed source and loaded-empty remain distinct. Map MultiResult diagnostics belong to the exact selected Result and its matching SHA; catalog groups do not infer a first child. Diagnostic read failures never become source error messages. Live compute state is a separate run-bound contract described by live-result-compute.

The existing mesh response carries deduplicated source NS/EW side arc identities. The preview joins only to matching complete finite arc paths from that same topology snapshot; parent draft, revision or selection changes retire it. Hover is view state and never creates a separate save path; edits remain in the child mesh ledger and parent geometry save.

The analysis tool explicitly chooses a saved project Result and loads actual inspector and plan-context providers. Acceptance checks the current project and source context, anchor revision and whole candidate groups before opening the existing keyed profile/map workspace. Dismiss the candidate picker before presenting the accepted workspace. This standalone route does not establish the original same-map Link Results active context or in-memory job support.

The retained managed reader catalogs the original condensed DSS paths and reads time series, paired curves and location records. Each host read checks the full-file source SHA and opens a byte-identical private copy, so a native open cannot create or update the user source. RecordType is distinct from DataType and units. Graphs preserve units groups, exact record/curve identities, irregular wall-time spacing and missing-value gaps; tables retain all quality words per sample. Wrong payloads, stale files, missing native libraries and unsupported kinds are explicit failures. The runtime is a separately built official pinned dependency package; its C/Fortran warning policy and acceptance are checked separately from C#/Swift builds. Managed native date strings use fixed English HEC formatting independent of the UI language. A private Unix stdout duplicate carries protocol JSON while native buffered diagnostic writes go to stderr.

Terrain plots use only selected source barrel IDs, clear on empty selection and keep duplicate names independent; each visible curve supplies its own length and coordinates. Quad mixed values may be explicitly unified only when the source permits Apply; mode mismatch must first be resolved through the source command. ConstantSize uses finite float values and PointCount uses Int32. Source refreshes update clean fields while preserving unsubmitted text; changed sources/selections and queued stale actions cannot apply old values. NS/EW hover previews resolve the selected source arc FIDs against the same revision/fingerprint map paths; dynamic result-map sampling is described by dynamic-map-profiles.

The project catalog opens the five original model kinds from the actual source catalog and asset collection. Geometry inputs target Terrain/NValue and Plan inputs target Geometry/BoundaryCondition. A link uses one unambiguous source kind/name identity and writes the existing project association draft; missing or duplicate names never pick the first object. Open/delete reuse the real catalog actions. Position edits use source filename-plus-suffix IDs, preserve unknown UML XML and pass through the shared visualization mutation lease and section-only receipt merge. Association drafts still require normal project Save. Native acceptance is separate.

A full catalog load or refresh resets all six single-value AND part filters and checks all returned types; All and a blank path component remain distinct. The type checked set supports none, partial and all, and newly introduced live types are checked. These filters operate only on actual provider records; the production provider now supplies source RecordType separately from DataType, and runtime/native UI acceptance is tracked independently. No synthetic records establish acceptance.

Mixed OpeningType selection stages the original force-set operation; KIn/KOut clear stages the retained NaN reset without dropping other raw fields. Apply submits commands in editable-field order to the exact selected property sets. Name/KInString/KOutString evaluate the retained ForwardedValidation attributes from ObservableOpeningProperties, including AbsoluteBounds(0,1); this is not a Swift range-check replacement. Per-keystroke source validation and generic ModelEditor field error adapters remain incomplete.

The native table delegates expression parsing and evaluation to retained Utility.Filtering, including logical operators, null checks, LIKE, IN and typed values. Original headers remain expression identifiers and first duplicate normalized headers win. An invalid expression retains the last accepted filter; a missing or nonfilterable field clears it. Queries never mutate model/project data, consume text drafts or replace source selection. Owner or row changes invalidate late replies. Source grid cell-range selection, some specialized chart-table adapters and full native acceptance remain separate work.

The UML writer receipt is accepted only for the captured saved visualization revision and exact current disk hash. Existing files must retain every non-UML section; only UML is merged into the live document, preserving pending Views and other local state. A first visualization file adopts non-Views sections without publishing pending Views. This merge contract alone does not establish a complete UML graph workflow or native acceptance.

Global topology shortcuts open the exact Geometry editor without loading over its dirty draft or inventing FIDs. The factor command preserves retained two-size and inverse-count arithmetic, and is grouped as one native draft history item. Recipes use the retained parser, source step fields and raw strings; mixed control points require explicit Force Set. Arc endpoint edits use the source shared node operation; internal points use exact arc and point ordinals. Unsubmitted coordinate and recipe buffers survive page replacement and participate in save/close guards independently of source dirty state. Native workflow acceptance remains separate.

Source-typed query evaluation retains same-definition OR, separate-definition and property AND, missing-tag versus null-property distinctions and original comparison fallback. Only the active Arc or Control Point list is filtered; filtering does not replace source selection or enter the topology mutation/undo/save ledger. Invalidated owners and late replies cannot install another Geometry result. UI wiring and provider checks do not establish complete native parity.

Terrain, Classification and local Gridded import reuse the primary editor and staged source services. The global chooser never loads or replaces an existing draft. Save/Discard/Cancel remains in the editor; only an accepted importer or explicit cancellation consumes the matching request. Global Tags choose arc or region and reach the same actual-FID metadata surface. The separate Cumulus provider branch remains unavailable. Source wiring alone does not establish native acceptance.

The global chooser uses the same retained Terrain/NValue style service as Map Layers, with distinct owner paths for repeated display names. A changed map, source selection or project rejects a late response. Global route availability does not expand the generic tool provider whitelist.

Only the two retained BC symbology definitions publish to the exact persisted Boundary owner. A missing unique line child may materialize beneath an existing BC. Apply preserves conditional/unknown XML and pending Views; explicit reset removes known local attributes even when effective values already equal global defaults. Runtime ShowStrokeVertices defaults false and follows the physical source owner while surviving a style-only context refresh. Selection and hover remain separate overlays. Conditional rules are not evaluated without a source attribute table.

Type defaults precede sparse overrides. Named/custom/manual/linear/histogram palettes retain source values; the initial NValue ramp ending at 1.0 is distinct from histogram fallback .1 and reset .16. Apply acquires the map mutation lease, verifies dependencies, commits only the exact .vis node and accepts its revision receipt before refreshing source context. Read cancellation cannot invalidate a submitted Apply. Classification keeps its discrete source rendering instead of using this continuous style form. Actual regression and native acceptance remain separately recorded.

Saved Plan maps remain separate from sidebar Plan mode. One focused Plan owns its Geometry and Boundary children; Matching Layers requires at least two focused Plans and retained common association semantics. Plan containers are not checkboxes. Focus, removal and Result insertion preserve sparse source XML. Map deletion uses an index-remap receipt to retain surviving runtime identities even when names repeat. validation remains separate from source relationship evidence.

The selected Result owns embedded Geometry and Boundary; equal current-project model names cannot substitute. Comparison choices stay in session state; exact SelectedMapType/ProfileIndex persist on the source row. Geometry maps retain embedded models directly below their Result as a native layout adaptation. Requests bind full source context and reject changed files, owners and late replies.

Project, Plan, Buildable, Geometry and selected Result rows load actual source coordinates and ordinals. Shared Plan associations have no singular ParentPlan. A Focused Plan Boundary child carries the exact ParentPlan plus a typed BoundaryCondition association; both model and association paths must match the captured source. Partial association or Result-owner fields cannot become a direct source. Nil-path source defaults are unchecked and hidden. Refresh rebuilds the current owner context. Exact-owner local/global line and vertex base styles now feed the real canvas; native style and runtime vertex controls live on the exact Boundary row. Conditional XML is preserved without inventing evaluation from feature ordinals; native acceptance remains separate.

Real Flow and OutletVelocity arrays pair with source barrel ordinal. Flow sign reverses travel; absolute flow below .001 draws a midpoint ring. VelocityScalar retains source bounds 1 through 1000 and default 25. Size and spawn timing use live map screen resolution independently of visible Result rasters. Only already-spawned live particles render, including long elapsed playback without total-spawn Int conversion. Controls are runtime state; live compute streaming and generic 2D particle controls remain incomplete.

The read-only service loads ClassicGeometry rather than modern Geometry, uses OverrideStationElevation ?? StationElevation and samples valid bank stations from that same profile. Only the override has a retained DatasetName attribute; reopening HDF does not fabricate transient computation profiles. Duplicate labels do not identify rows. Linked windows follow the latest selection; pinned windows keep their own row. Source/project changes invalidate old contexts, late replies cannot replace current selection, and viewing creates no HDF or project writes. The original CrossSection action dispatcher remains unestablished; the native entry explicitly chooses a source file.

The sidebar Geometry filter is separate from a saved Geometry map. Focus creates or updates the source map tree in original focus order, with Focused Geometries, Matching Layers and Layers roots. Buildable membership belongs under Layers. Child checks and styles remain owned by that exact map. Source integration and native workflow acceptance are recorded separately; a compiled batch does not establish complete UI parity.

Equal display names do not establish associations. The retained source objects and samplers produce real viewport pixels and original category/ramp colors. Hidden, empty, unavailable and failed remain distinct. Panning changes the token; stale or cancelled replies cannot retain an old frame. Plan and Result association-owner expansion is work; native workflow acceptance remains separate.

Incomplete text and complete business-error candidates remain outside source fields and ordered Plan time-window mutations. They survive page replacement, block save/compute/tool execution, and clear on explicit discard/reload. Verified setter/peer routes reproduce source window warnings and fixed-start boundary errors; a pending peer must never fall back to its old valid source value.

Embedded Plan values never resolve through a same-named current-project Plan. The picker carries whole source groups into a real linked workspace. Retained KeyedProfileState uses the first result timeline and 10 ms tolerance; unmatched children stay unavailable and nearest indices are informational. Common map rendering consumes these exact indices; unavailable summary frames remain explicit source capabilities.

Association targets contain HDF models only. N-value choices require the actual NValues category. Physical host paths map back to original asset IDs without changing relative project-path resolution. Conflicting physical identities reject the catalog; a missing current association remains visible.

Dropped files enter the same inspect/preview/import queue as the native file picker. The request carries the source ProjectBackwards/ProjectForwards choice with ProjectBackwards as its omitted default. The retained source stores this UI choice but applies no corresponding projection algorithm or HDF field, so import preserves selected band timestamps. Unknown values reject before publication.

Catalog previews open the selected source instead of borrowing the active map or an editor draft. Terrain and Classification requests carry only the snapshot source revision/state with no read-only fields submitted as edits. Result profiles preserve the owning project path as the base for relative dependencies. Cancellation and request generations reject a previous selection.

Dataset selection, axis units, date/log formatting, cursor intersections, bounds, zoom, tick density, fonts and table state belong to one chart. Source identity or values reset old view state. Legend overlay is the source global preference and uses macOS UserDefaults; other options stay local. Coarse wheel events use a pointer anchor; precise trackpad events retain native scrolling. Presentation changes never enter model persistence. Plot pixel sizing and logarithmic tick parity remain partial.

Read and Apply target only the current map and project BoundaryCondition, excluding embedded Result/MultiResult contexts. Presence-aware local ARGB attributes inherit application defaults. A changed global default updates only a whole option still equal to its former default. Apply rejects a stale captured global revision, preserves unknown XML, conditional rules and pending Views, and never writes HDF. Boundary conditional evaluation remains incomplete.

Twenty-five unique definition IDs retain twenty-seven declaration variants; duplicate polyline IDs remain one preference key. A complete valid replacement persists atomically in macOS UserDefaults. Global reset clears only that dictionary. Source text comparison omitted font size and emphasis; native equality retains both. Global preferences must not write project XML, HDF or map .vis.

Read and save resolve the exact retained MapLayer, never the first equal filename. A changed option writes all attributes exposed by its source type; an option equal to captured global defaults omits the entire attribute group. Four ordered condition groups preserve source enum operator names on disk and UI tokens in memory. Unknown XML and pending local Views survive an atomic saved-baseline merge. GDB identity parsing exists but its production file loading route remains incomplete.

Columns retain string, Int32, Int64, Single, Double or unsupported source types, including original mixed-number promotion to string. Each property applies the first matching ordered rule. The renderer consumes per-feature results only with a verified source ordinal; display attributes and FID values are not a join key. Unsaved geometry edits invalidate that proof. Shapefile, GDB and specialized Topology state conditions remain separate incomplete routes.

The linked profile service supplies exact child frame indices; each Result renders its own embedded geometry and associated terrain through the shared CPU renderer. One response owns every overlay in the common viewport. Minimum is unavailable; Maximum requires actual Legacy summary datasets, with no first/last or nearest-profile substitution.

Only the source mismatch command may reset KIn or KOut to NaN. It uses a typed mutation replayed by the original ObservableOpeningProperties setters, with undo and the parent HDF save/discard boundary. Ordinary numeric input continues to reject nonfinite values; reset is not an empty-string edit or a generic numeric-parser exception.

The summary picker calls the parent editor selection callback, including Save/Discard/Cancel. Terrain and N-value associations remain Project XML drafts. Only HDF model files enter association choices; backing TIFF/vector inputs stay browsable without becoming model rows. Only source-classified NValues enter the N-value picker. Re-evaluating the same geometry under changed ProjectXML replays pending mesh mutations rather than retiring the draft, while source generations reject late earlier-context replies. Prepare summary is the retained GeometryMesh stored summary, not inferred readiness.

Directory, version and data location come from the initialized retained GDAL setup/native library. Portable expected locations describe current platform/package lookup. The toolbar and focused macOS command open the same native sheet; close cancels the request and rejects late data. Source Windows installation hints are replaced by actual host paths.

The GeoJSON AST preserves unknown properties and extra coordinate ordinates. Each map owns its selected component and draft. Async mutations recheck source SHA and the shared-file edit gate immediately before committing. Save All and close/replacement include unfinished sketches and explicit Save/Discard. Split and endpoint attachment retain extra ordinates; merge is limited to components of one MultiLineString so unrelated feature metadata cannot be discarded. Source raster sampling, cross-feature merge and non-GeoJSON edits remain incomplete.

Active sources require checked ancestors. MultiResult choices come from current Project Results matched to the embedded Plan name; source selection normalization and multiple contiguous slots are retained. Overrides remain map session state because the original serializer does not persist them. Source snapshots fingerprint project XML, visualization and all candidate result files. Native setup coalesces concurrent requests by full map workflow identity plus exact requested slot overrides. Session-owned source completion is independent of cancellable callers; configuration/invalidation cancels the old generation. Pending source selections settle before dependent setup, which requires an accepted same-map/same-workflow snapshot. First/new accepted source contexts notify Store even when Latest overrides stay empty; same-token refreshes do not requeue configuration. Retirement checks never create a missing map state. Hidden Result-owned Boundary rows do not request an active owner; visible rows retain exact source/slot guards. The result-source completion identity is installed only after source-tree/vector, Geometry, associated and Boundary configuration finishes. Cancelled or superseded replies cannot install stale bindings or surface an obsolete setup error. Build, regression and native acceptance remain separately recorded.

Each chart freezes exact native component coordinates and active source selection slots. Source callbacks compute the real series, including retained accumulated-volume integration. A changed map, line, draft or source invalidates the chart; window close cancels and unregisters its own request. The Result post-processing cache side effect is declared.

Each node owns a separate timeline. MultiResult selects matching timestamps from the first selection key within the original tolerance. The retained renderer samples all source flow areas and associated terrain, keeps actual units, source color ramp and NoData, and rejects changed dependencies. Viewport generations publish ordered node overlays together. A stable map reference prevents sampled viewport bounds from rebasing the map.

Result add/remove uses original Buildable Result/MultiResult membership; Project results remain source generated. GeoJSON import creates the real point/line/polygon buckets; visible buckets and ancestor visibility apply per map. Map-wide result type persists original SelectedMapType names. Unknown visualization data and unsaved Project XML stay preserved.

One source file is read once per unique physical path, then each persisted vector-family node receives its own filtered render identity, name and ancestor-derived visibility. Source feature/component IDs, geometry paths, source ordinals, attributes, URL and SHA remain those of the shared file. A pending same-file GeoJSON draft is projected into each matching instance. Production support here is GeoJSON/JSON only; other source vector formats remain separate.

Reads and saves bind to a canonical local file while the original layer URL remains its display identity. Async edits verify the source after awaits and recheck the per-file shared-edit gate immediately before draft mutation. Save captures bytes and generation, coordinates an atomic replacement only when the expected SHA still matches, and acknowledges only the same current scope. Save All, close and project replacement include unsaved edits and unfinished sketches. These checks are source-static integration evidence, not runtime acceptance.

The retained ComboBox binds its ordered Units to ItemsSource, SelectedUnit to SelectedValue, and SelectedValue changes back to SelectedUnit. SwiftUI retains source order, presents each source Name, writes the exact unit ID, and keeps a missing persisted ID visible until the user chooses a current option. Selection is presentation state; numeric edits convert through the source affine conversion and remain explicit model drafts.

The .vis file stores the Geometry node by type/name and does not prove which physical model owns it. A local sketch blocks save, discard, close and asset replacement while keeping Apply/Cancel usable. New lines use the real associated terrain extent; reshaping retains source coordinates. Generic deletion of all model kinds and source LinkFocus remain separate incomplete work.

Map writers, raster style writers and result removal are mutually exclusive. Source pin serialization is unavailable; Plan/Geometry trees retain the read-only fallback until their map contexts are implemented.

Flow areas retain source row ordinals scoped to the HDF revision; region control points retain source FIDs. Mesh preview overlays the current topology ledger. Original patch rules and source mesh generation run in memory; retained operations join the parent staged save after topology replay. A topology change cannot silently apply an older mesh ledger. Mesh error thresholds and selection are view state.

Culvert field edits and property-set operations replay through original observable APIs. Draft-created property sets retain UUID identities rather than display names. Culvert edits share one staged parent HDF publication with topology, mesh, ordinary fields and images.

Result plan, geometry, boundary conditions, compute summary and output-block metadata come from the selected Result file. Same-name current project models do not replace embedded snapshots. Terrain override changes only the current project XML draft; inspection never saves the result. Missing output or compute metadata stays missing.

The profile reader uses actual stored source HDF datasets with original profile timestamps, cell or face identity and the embedded result unit system. Selection and request generations prevent late responses from replacing a different result or element. Empty or absent datasets are explicitly unavailable; source writer fixtures are test data rather than solver acceptance.

Original model defaults are written to a staged source HDF and published under the source project directory without overwriting another file. The project XML draft is carried into model metadata but is not saved implicitly. The creation sheet prevents cancellation during publication; successful output refreshes the actual catalog and opens the correct editor.

Busy topology, mesh or culvert operations cannot be discarded by close, project replacement or application termination. One child's clean callback cannot clear another child or ordinary draft. Old save completion cannot acknowledge a new asset. Save-all still publishes individual files sequentially rather than as one global transaction.

An explicit read-only check applies canonical plan time-window state and ordered events plus ordinary draft fields against current project XML. Source CanCompute returns actual result, codes, severities, ordered log values and aggregated counts. Selected model dependency hashes and existence states are checked before/after. A reply cannot install after edit, reload, discard, association change or source revision change. Checking neither saves nor prepares a solver job.

Arc polylines, completed-region outer/inner rings, control points and nodes use actual source coordinates. Compound region boundaries retain source row selection IDs without inventing a single FID. Even-odd rendering/hit testing preserves holes. Pan/zoom remain view state; tag/size refresh keeps camera extent and existing child draft save semantics.

Typed BaseUnitType IDs identify source/display units without guessing a family from unit labels. Temporary calculator edits call the retained conversion service; cancel does not write. Explicit apply revalidates original owner, field, unit and raw value before scoped draft commit. Interval normalization preserves the original 100 ns TimeSpan rounding; display formatting does not truncate stored precision.

The shell displays every current message with severity, title, body, timestamp and per-item dismissal. Source timeout scales UTF-16 length and clamps to 25..100 percent of ten seconds. Hover pauses remaining lifetime, disappearing suspends timers, dismissed/expired IDs do not replay; history stays in the workspace. Caller-supplied actions use actual Messages navigation rather than a generic success stub.

Source FIDs identify features independently of sorted rows. Typed tags, metadata, Arc and Region user-defined column add/rename/delete, and quick sizing replay against the original geometry in memory. Column permissions use the source Arc or ControlPoint default-column predicate and observable metadata-table APIs; Nodes expose no column CRUD. Arc sizing follows its Constant or Count function; regions and Quad sides use their source rules. The child draft joins ordinary geometry fields and images in one staged HDF save. Save locks the child, acknowledges only its captured draft and rebases its revision. Discard, model replacement and late replies cannot restore an obsolete draft.

Catalog and professional project trees have separate source hierarchies and separate sessions. Current unsaved XML supplies associations. Model nodes retain actual asset paths, backups and source component identities. Maps retain their own IDs and original types. Unsupported tree mutations remain unavailable rather than reporting a saved change.

The visualization node supplies original relative-first filenames. Every source request validates its exact map and node and samples the actual GDAL raster through retained resampling and color-fill logic. Apply renders actual pixels before atomically publishing visualization XML. Custom palettes share the original global catalog. Native baseline acceptance verifies old and new visualization revisions and preserves unsaved Views. Source-map IDs isolate pixels and extents between maps; source changes require an explicit reload.

The retained BaseUnitType catalog defines compatible families and performs conversion. Editing the source value converts forward; editing the target value or changing its unit converts backward. Changing the source family invalidates incompatible target choices. G8 is presentation only; raw input and full stored values survive formatting and invalid intermediate input.

Opt-in newline JSON streams source messages and actual reported percentages while legacy responses remain supported. Pipe chunks are buffered as bytes until a whole frame is available. Exactly one terminal response is accepted. Cancellation terminates the actual request child and late UI callbacks are ignored. The migration result preserves source messages and checks the project revision again before presenting an explicit Open action.

Mode and date changes replay in order through the retained observable setters. Opaque source state preserves inactive internal dates while boundary inheritance displays actual boundary dates. Time-window fields bypass generic dirty-field overlay. Refresh baseline excludes user state; discard restores that baseline. Save acknowledges only captured event IDs and rebases later events onto the new saved source revision.

The selected asset loads its own source summary schema and metadata through the existing model provider. This read does not register an editor or replace any editor draft. N-value and classification kinds derive from actual source schemas. Stale selection replies cannot overwrite the current summary; professional previews require real selected-node render data.

Inspect validates the retained v6 project header and proposes an unused output folder. The retained ModelConverter writes a separate project; success requires one top-level RAS file. Cancellation terminates the one-request backend child and may retain partial output. The current workspace and drafts stay live until success; replacement confirmation happens after the migration sheet dismisses.

The source editor displays only MaxValue and MinValue using three-significant-digit NumberConverters formatting. A provider must supply the actual fill color values; generic raster limits or editable palette draft stops cannot substitute for that context.

Project maps follow loaded project layers. Buildable maps begin empty and include only explicitly added layer IDs. URL import and tree drop capture the destination map; hidden layers, viewport and membership stay per map. Professional model tree listeners remain unconnected.

Refresh evaluates source getters against current unsaved project XML without writing any files. Baseline excludes user drafts; draft applies validated setters. Aliases, exact raw input and images remain dirty. Old replies cannot replace later typing, reload, discard or save; association changes during save are deferred.

Priority display reverses real source order. Local selection is navigation-only. Renames, functional expressions, constants and extents are scoped drafts. Source transforms preserve the original discard baseline. Removed rasters remain in the dependency ledger. Explicit staged HDF save rebases selected input identity and resets the source layer input hash. Source sampling provides the actual raster preview; unsupported input types remain intact.

Separate per-source structure review from backend execution and native acceptance. An unreviewed control is not assumed absent. Supplementary code-created controls and backing objects remain outside the 517-class resource baseline. Run audit-ui-rewrite.py after edits; schema extraction alone does not establish a translated screen.

Chrome collapse, move, resize, placement, opacity and visibility are view state. Undo/redo is enabled only when a provider supplies actual edit history capabilities. Scale labels remain map-coordinate units until a real projection-aware length conversion is provided; do not infer metres from project display units.

The retained layer samples a 256x256 presentation raster from current source inputs and drafts. Colors map actual class names, NoData is transparent. Map replies are scoped to asset/load/edit revisions; source raster dependencies are rechecked. Fit/pan/zoom are navigation, not model edits.

Create/replace/delete mutate actual source polygons in memory. Batch delete is one undo step. Original feature IDs survive earlier deletions; new features receive GUIDs. Replay preserves class overrides and independent metadata. XY edits retain optional Z/M arrays and nonfinite ordinate strings. Drawing selects only new features; save rebases feature selection by source/input ordinal. Explicit source HDF save establishes a new undo baseline; discard restores saved geometry.

Missing flags retain legacy dimension inference; float XYZ is decoded. Source regression covers mixed polygons/polylines and legacy layouts.

Import saves captured model drafts and new inputs through a staged HDF. Failed batches remove only owned new rasters. Native sheet identity carries selected files atomically.

Stable editor IDs derive from asset revision and original input ordinal. Selection is navigation-only; reorder/removal preserve independent field/table drafts and the original discard baseline. Polygon inputs remain nonremovable. Explicit save rebases IDs while retaining the selected source input.

Names persist from input definitions; mapping/name hashes participate in source dirty detection and reset after successful save. Raster dependency SHA checks guard structural transforms and staged HDF saves.

Classification choices use file paths; HDF persists source names. Opening does not reconcile or prune mappings. Explicit changes use original class-map reconciliation, preserving common values and adding new names with zero. None clears the actual association and table.

The original twenty NLCD values update matching names only; custom classes remain unchanged. Operations retain metadata/image drafts and the saved discard baseline. Explicit save writes the actual HDF table; dependency hashes reject changed classification files.

Retained GDAL summaries and selection builders supply actual bands. The source scalar/vector/precipitation importers write canonical values and timestamps; independent wind components and NoData are preserved.
A frame changes only its spatial presentation. It cannot install draft fields as a saved baseline or replace point/payload state. Import is an explicit model-save operation.

Scalar station values and both wind components retain original units. Regular times are derived; absolute/relative irregular arrays retain subsecond precision. Charts cannot be sent as edits for table-backed pages. Station/input structural records remain in the editor draft until explicit HDF save.

A valid Local projection writes no fabricated .prj.

Both canvas hits and filtered feature rows capture the same menu context and share one action dispatcher. Preserve an already-selected set or add under Control. Export actual centers or perimeter polylines with typed original attributes and project CRS.
